newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S. boosts Kuwait defence by deploying Patriots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. boosts Kuwait defence by deploying Patriots.

text.p: The United States has sent a battery of Patriot air defence missile launchers to Kuwait to strengthen its Gulf Arab ally's defences against former occupier Iraq, U.S. officials said on Wednesday.
"They (Patriots) provide theatre missile defence," U.S. military spokesman Lieutenant Colonel Thomas Nickerson said.
Nickerson would not say when the battery and its 100-strong operational and maintenance crew had arrived but added they had been moved from another location in the Arabian peninsula.
"You might see them today but you might not see them tomorrow. We like to keep moving them," he added.
Another U.S. official who declined to be identified said the launchers "arrived earlier this week".

The United States earlier this month sent two Patriot anti-missile batteries and U.S. soldiers to Saudi Arabia after Iraq fired missiles at U.S. warplanes last week in the latest military confrontation between Washington and Baghdad.
Washington last week sent eight Stealth bombers and more than 20 other warplanes to Kuwait in a display of force aimed at containing what it sees as Iraqi threats to the oil-rich region.
More than 1,100 U.S. Army troops were already in Kuwait for desert exercises when the latest standoff with Baghdad began.

In the next few days these forces will be joined by 3,500 additional troops being sent by President Bill Clinton to expand a U.S. display of force aimed at containing what Washington sees as Iraqi threats to the region.
Reporters in Kuwait saw a number of Patriot launchers near a military facility north of Kuwait City but it was not immediately known if they were the newly-arrived U.S. units.
A Patriot battery normally consists of eight launchers.
Kuwait has taken delivery of some of the Patriot launchers it ordered after the 1991 Gulf War but military analysts say these are not yet fully operational.
Patriot missiles were used as defence against Iraqi Scud missiles during the 1991 Gulf War that ended a seven-month Iraqi occupation of Kuwait.
